words.g: m. nom. sg. of मार्कण्डेय (taddhita: ‘descendant of Mṛkaṇḍu’); subject of उवाच
√वच् (adādi, 2P ‘to speak’), liṭ (perfect), prathama-puruṣa ekavacana, kartari prayoga

sandhi.note: -aḥ before a vowel other than a: the visarga becomes y, the y is dropped, and the two vowels stand apart (मार्कण्डेय | उवाच). The gap is not closed again.

morph.note: Perfect of √वच्: reduplication उ-वाच with samprasāraṇa of the reduplicated syllable (व → उ). The perfect is the narrative past of the Purāṇas: ‘(he) said’.

mantras.anvaya_en: Subject and verb: a speaker label.

comm.t: The speaker label that opens the Devī Māhātmya. In the Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa the sage Mārkaṇḍeya is answering his pupil Krauṣṭuki’s questions about the ages of the Manus; the whole of the Devī Māhātmya is a story told inside that answer.

The Gita Press pāṭha counts every uvāca line as a mantra, which is how the text reaches seven hundred (the chapter colophons count them separately: 57 uvāca mantras in all). In recitation this first mantra carries the bījas ॐ ऐं, which belong to the pāṭha, not to the Purāṇa.

words.g: m. nom. sg. of मनु (u-stem); predicate of कथ्यते

ordinal of अष्टन्, m. nom. sg.; qualifies मनुः
नि + √शम् (causative stem निशामय- ‘to perceive’), loṭ (imperative), madhyama-puruṣa ekavacana, parasmaipada
f. acc. sg.; compound (see Samāsa); object of निशामय
m. abl. sg. of विस्तर, used adverbially
present participle (śatṛ) of √गद् ‘to speak’, m. gen. sg.; agrees with मम
first-person pronoun अस्मद्, gen. sg.; ‘hear from me’ (the speaker heard is in the genitive)

sandhi.note: -aḥ before a voiced consonant becomes -o: the visarga (as रु) turns to u, and a + u gives o. The same change gives यो मनुः and गदतो मम.
A word-final e before initial a: the a is absorbed into the e. The avagraha (ऽ) marks the lost a.
Final t becomes d before a voiced sound (here g). The Gita Press writes the d with a virāma and a space.
The pronoun stem tat ends in d before the vowel of उत्पत्ति. The final m of the compound becomes anusvāra before the next word’s v (मोऽनुस्वारः, 8.3.23).

samasa.sense: how Sāvarṇi came to be — the story that follows

morph.note: Passive present: stem कथ्य- (√कथ् + yak) with the ātmanepada ending -ते. ‘Is called’; the Manu is the grammatical subject.
Imperative of the causative stem of नि + √शम्, a Purāṇic idiom for ‘listen’ (literally ‘perceive’).
Present participle गदत् (√गद् + śatṛ), genitive singular: ‘of (me) telling’. With verbs of hearing the source is put in the genitive.

mantras.anvaya: यः सूर्यतनयः सावर्णिः अष्टमः मनुः कथ्यते, तदुत्पत्तिं विस्तरात् गदतः मम निशामय।
mantras.anvaya_en: A relative clause (यः … कथ्यते) names the subject; the main clause is the imperative निशामय with its object तदुत्पत्तिम्, and गदतः मम gives the speaker.
mantras.lit: Sāvarṇi, the son of the Sun, who is called the eighth Manu — hear his origin from me as I tell it in detail.
mantras.tr: Sāvarṇi, the Sun’s son, is spoken of as the eighth Manu. Listen as I tell you at length how he came to be.

comm.t: Mārkaṇḍeya announces his subject: the origin of Sāvarṇi, the eighth Manu. The frame closes in the last mantra of the text (13.29), where King Suratha is promised rebirth from the Sun as Sāvarṇi. The glory of the Goddess is told as the answer to a question about a Manu.
The chapter colophons place the text in the Purāṇa’s account of the Sāvarṇika manvantara (सावर्णिके मन्वन्तरे). Each Manu presides over one age of the world; the eighth age is still to come.
A modern reading: the Goddess first appears inside an ordinary story of loss and succession. Grace, in this text, works through history, not around it.

sandhi.note: ā + a: two like vowels merge into one long ā.

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi inside a compound (yaṇ and savarṇa-dīrgha)
sandhi.note: u before a vowel becomes v (मनु + अन्तर → मन्वन्तर); a + a → ā (अन्तर + अधिप → अन्तराधिप).
The visarga of सः (and एषः) is dropped before any consonant.
Visarga before t becomes s; then तनयः before the voiced r of रवेः becomes तनयो (हशि च, 6.1.114).

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (its first member महामाया is itself a karmadhāraya: महती चासौ माया च)
samasa.literal: by the might of the Great Māyā
samasa.sense: by the Goddess’s grace — the first time the text names her

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (मन्वन्तर = मनोः अन्तरम्, also ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa)
samasa.sense: the Manu who presides over an age

morph.note: Perfect of √भू with the reduplicated syllable ब (bh → b). With a predicate nominative it means ‘became’: स … मन्वन्तराधिपः बभूव.

mantras.anvaya: रवेः तनयः महाभागः सः सावर्णिः महामायानुभावेन यथा मन्वन्तराधिपः बभूव, (तत् शृणु)।
mantras.anvaya_en: A dependent clause of manner (यथा … बभूव) still governed by निशामय in 1.2: ‘(hear) how he became …’.
mantras.lit: How, by the power of Mahāmāyā, that greatly fortunate Sāvarṇi, son of Ravi, became lord of a manvantara —
mantras.tr: Hear how, by the grace of Mahāmāyā, that blessed Sāvarṇi, son of the Sun, came to rule an age of the world.
mantras.tr_note: The verse continues the sentence of 1.2; ‘Hear’ is supplied from निशामय there.

comm.t: The cause of Sāvarṇi’s rise is stated at once: the power (अनुभाव) of Mahāmāyā. The story of Suratha that follows (1.4 onward) explains how.

Mahāmāyā is the name under which the first carita knows the Goddess: the power that binds beings in attachment (1.55–58) and the power that releases them. The same name returns in Medhas’s teaching (1.55) and in Brahmā’s hymn.
Lalitā Sahasranāma (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa) also names her Mahāmāyā (name 215, महामाया). The shared name is a shared idea in Śākta thought; the two texts remain separate works.

sandhi.note: -e + a- → -e’-: the initial a is elided (avagraha).
After राजा + अभूत् → राजाभूत्, the final t of अभूत् stays unvoiced before the unvoiced s; the words are only written together.

samasa.vigraha: चैत्रस्य वंशः चैत्रवंशः; चैत्रवंशे समुद्भवः यस्य सः
samasa.literal: whose birth is in Caitra’s line
samasa.sense: a king of the Caitra dynasty
samasa.alt: Also read as a saptamī tatpuruṣa, चैत्रवंशे समुद्भवः, ‘one born in Caitra’s line’; the sense is the same.

samasa.literal: in the circle of the earth

morph.note: Root aorist of √भू with augment a-: ‘was, came to be’. Used alongside the perfect for narrative past.
Taddhita derivative: स्वारोचिष ‘belonging to Svarocis’, i.e. the age of the second Manu, Svārociṣa.

mantras.anvaya: पूर्वं स्वारोचिषे अन्तरे चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवः सुरथः नाम राजा समस्ते क्षितिमण्डले अभूत्।
mantras.anvaya_en: Time (पूर्वं स्वारोचिषे अन्तरे), subject with its epithet (चैत्रवंशसमुद्भवः सुरथः नाम राजा), place (समस्ते क्षितिमण्डले), verb (अभूत्).
mantras.lit: Formerly, in the Svārociṣa interval, there was over the whole circle of the earth a king named Suratha, born in Caitra’s line.
mantras.tr: Long ago, in the age of Svārociṣa Manu, there lived a king named Suratha, of the line of Caitra, who ruled the whole earth.

comm.t: Suratha is introduced: a universal king of an earlier age. The story will take everything from him, in order (1.5–9).

Suratha is the king who, at the end of the text, receives his kingdom back and is promised birth as Sāvarṇi (13.25–29). His companion, the merchant Samādhi, will ask for knowledge instead. The tradition reads the pair as the two goals the Goddess grants: enjoyment (bhoga) and liberation (mokṣa).
